investigations.name: draft-to-living-cell
investigations.title: From Draft to Living Cell
investigations.question: Does the paper's central claim hold in executable form — that a biological interface can be treated as a modeling choice and a testable hypothesis, so that composing heterogeneous, independently-built simulators through one typed interface per pattern reproduces the paper's cellular composition patterns? And does the same interface survive being realized by very different mechanisms behind it — a Cellular Potts cell versus a lumped-ODE cell, dynamic flux-balance analysis versus a lumped Michaelis-Menten kinetic — as the paper's substitutability claim predicts? The subject here is the interface; process bigraphs (Vivarium) are the example substrate we use to make it executable.
investigations.hypothesis: The paper's composition patterns are properties of the interfaces, not of any particular mechanism behind them. One typed coupling process per pattern is enough to compose independently-built frameworks (viva-cpm, spatio-flux) without either one knowing about the other; each study is a behavior-gated test of an interface hypothesis, passing or failing on genuine simulation output rather than a scripted trajectory; and where the same interface is realized by two different mechanisms the externally observable relation is preserved — an executable instance of the paper's equivalence-class claim.
